title: Regular locus is open when every prime quotient has a regular open
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] contains a nonempty open subset $U_{\mathfrak p}$ such that $(A/\mathfrak p)_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every $\mathfrak q\in U_{\mathfrak p}$. Then $\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A:A_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Tag 07P9, lemma-intersection-regular-with-closed; J-0 and J-1 expanded using Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: For primes q ≤ p with A_p regular, use the prime correspondence to obtain Q in A_p contracting to q. Localize the regular local ring A_p at Q and transport regularity along the canonical localization-of-localization isomorphism to A_q. This proves generalization stability.

At a regular prime p, take a finite generating set of the maximal ideal of A_p with cardinal its spanFinrank d. Regularity identifies d with its Krull dimension. Represent each generator as a fraction f_i/t_i; membership in the maximal ideal gives f_i in p, and multiplying by the denominator units preserves the generated ideal. The resulting d numerators form a regular system of parameters and therefore a regular sequence.

Spread this regular sequence to A_g for some g outside p. Put I = (f_i). Choose finite generators of p. Since I and p have equal extensions to A_p, clear the denominator for each generator and multiply the resulting elements outside p. The product s is outside p and satisfies s a in I for every a in p, by linearity and the span of the generators.

Choose a principal open D(bbar) containing a point of the assumed nonempty regular open in Spec(A/p), and contained in that open. Lift bbar to b in A. Since D(bbar) is nonempty, b is outside p. For every prime q containing p and avoiding b, the prime qbar = q/p lies in this principal open. Its localization is regular. The quotient of A_q by p A_q is a localization of A/p at qbar, so the canonical localization equivalence makes that quotient regular local.

Let k = g s b, outside p, and fix a prime q containing p and avoiding k. Then g, s, b are outside q. The inclusion of the powers of g into the complement of q exhibits A_q as a localization of A_g. Preservation of weak regularity localizes the sequence from A_g to A_q; the tower of algebra maps identifies its entries with f_i/1. Each entry lies in the maximal ideal because f_i is in p contained in q, so the local regular-sequence criterion upgrades weak regularity to regularity.

In A_q, the ideal generated by f_i/1 is p A_q: I is contained in p, while s a in I for each a in p and s/1 is a unit. Identify this ideal with Ideal.ofList of the regular sequence. The quotient is regular by the preceding quotient-localization argument. A_q is Noetherian and local, so lifting regularity from a regular-sequence quotient proves A_q regular. Thus k gives a principal neighbourhood inside V(p).

Apply Nagata’s criterion to the predicate on ideals asserting that the ideal is prime and its localization is regular local. The proved generalization and closed-subset neighbourhood properties supply its hypotheses. Every regular prime therefore has a principal open neighbourhood entirely of regular primes. Since principal opens are open, the regular locus is open. The argument is vacuous for an empty spectrum and handles the empty parameter sequence without exception.
